html:
Basutoland was the British territory in the Maloti mountains of southern Africa that became the Kingdom of Lesotho. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

The Basotho nation was built by Moshoeshoe I, who gathered refugees of the Mfecane wars at his mountain stronghold of Thaba Bosiu in the 1820s. In the 1850s and 1860s the Boers of the Orange Free State took much of his best farmland in a series of wars. To save the rest, Moshoeshoe asked for British protection, granted in 1868.

From 1871 the Cape Colony ruled it. When the Cape tried to disarm the Basotho, they rose in the Gun War of 1880 and 1881 and won. In 1884 Britain took the territory back under direct rule, which kept it out of South Africa when the Union formed in 1910. Many Basotho men worked in the mines of Kimberley and Johannesburg. Independence came in 1966.
